originalTitle: Australia news live: Australia sends firefighters to France as blazes rage; leaders gather for Garma festival
content: Albanese goes on one week of leave Prime minister Anthony Albanese is taking a week of leave, his office has announced, with Richard Marles acting in his stead. “The Prime Minister will be on leave from Friday 31 July until Thursday 6 August 2026,” reads a statement posted on Albanese’s website. During this time, the Deputy Prime Minister will be Acting Prime Minister. Gina Rinehart responds after report she lobbied to move 2032 Olympic rowing to crocodile-inhabited river Gina Rinehart has responded to a report yesterday that she had lobbied for a controversial plan to move the 2032 Olympic rowing events to the Fitzroy River in Rockhampton, a natural habitat for saltwater crocodiles. The Guardian’s Ben Smee reports the decision prompted significant backlash. A spokesperson for Hancock Prospecting said in a statement yesterday: Mrs Rinehart has also for decades been a huge champion of regional Australia and her insights expressed in the letter were done so for the reason of outlining the benefits hosting Olympic events would bring to a regional town like Rockhampton. Too often regional towns are forgotten. Given that Mrs Rinehart is also the Patron of Rowing Australia, has been involved in the sport for many years, and she knows Queensland well, so it’s hardly surprising that she would offer insight on this matter, as other similar sporting representatives also did. To suggest she has done so for any ulterior motive or to gain any kind of personal benefit is completely false! Conservationists say massive marine park expansion ‘a win’ for the ocean Marine conservationists have said a federal government plan to massively expand marine park areas around two remote islands will be a win for the ocean. The environment minister, Murray Watt, has announced this morning the government wants to add an area almost 10 times the size of Tasmania to marine parks around Norfolk Island and Lord Howe Island that would ban fishing and mining. Fiona Maxwell, oceans manager at Pew Charitable Trusts, said the proposal “represents a huge step forward in protecting Australia’s extraordinary marine life”. Paul Gamblin, the chief executive of the Australian Marine Conservation Society, said the step would “safeguard these underwater wonderlands” but the action needed to be replicated across federal waters. Proposal to add area almost 10 times size of Tasmania to two remote marine parks The Albanese government wants to ban fishing and mining from an extra 671,500 square kilometres of ocean around Norfolk Island and Lord Howe Island – an area almost 10 times the size of Tasmania. The proposal is part of a review of 44 marine parks and, if it survives the current consultation period unscathed, would see the government reach its target to have at least 30% of Australia’s ocean estate in highly protected marine park zones by 2030. The government said the two marine parks, hundreds of kilometres off Australia’s east coast, were ecologically significant as they supported a mix of cool and tropical marine habitats and were important corridors for migratory seabirds, cetaceans, fish and sharks. Glenn Baker, an Australian music journalist and rock historian, has died at the age of 74, his longtime friend and collaborator said this morning. A tribute posted to Baker’s Facebook page this morning reads: Glenn’s contribution to the Australian rock ’n’ roll music landscape was immense, but his family remembers him as a loving father of six and grandfather of thirteen. Glenn’s passion for music, travel, food and his family (still not entirely sure of the order) was, like his personality, larger than life. Baker’s son, Orson, told The Sydney Morning Herald this morning his father had an “amazing life”. He was so deeply involved in the music industry that we are talking about a man who absolutely had a life fully lived. Rose Davies makes history in Australian 5,000m one-two at Commonwealth Games In the fading Glasgow light, the two fluorescent yellow figures powered around the final bend of the 5,000m at the Commonwealth Games, leaving the rest of the field behind. Megan Keith, the young Scot who had broken the field apart with a mile to go, could not keep up. Behind her was Kenya’s last hope of making it six 5,000m women’s golds in a row, Caroline Nyaga, as well as Ugandan Esther Chebet and England’s Hannah Nuttall. All of them, now irrelevant. Australian Rose Davies had stayed within this leading group for the entire race, before surging past Keith with 200m to go. History was in her grasp: a woman had never done the 10,000m-5,000m double at the Commonwealth Games. Read more here: The parents of an Australian man facing the possible death penalty in Syria spoke to the ABC last night, saying diplomatic efforts to aid their son had not been fruitful. Patrick Stevenson, 20, has been detained for seven months over the alleged shooting death of another Australian, Abdullah Glen Charles Burgess in December. Angela Bell, Stevenson’s mother, told the ABC she was disappointed in her dealings with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (Dfat) so far. Bell told ABC’s 7.30 program: They say … that their policy is that he shouldn’t have been travelling to Syria … and that’s where the conversation gets stuck. They use the word ‘limited’ a lot. They don’t use the word failure, but basically the sense is they … have limited capacity to help in this situation. Bell said she hadn’t seen a “single document” detailing the charges against her son, and there was “no access” to him. Prime minister Anthony Albanese said yesterday while legal processes would “take their course overseas”, the government was providing support for Stevenson’s family. chineseContent: 阿尔巴内塞将休假一周 总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞的办公室宣布，他将休假一周，由理查德·马勒斯接替。 Albanese 网站上发布的一份声明称：“总理将于 7 月 31 日星期五至 2026 年 8 月 6 日星期四休假。”在此期间，副总理将担任代总理。吉娜·莱因哈特 (Gina Rinehart) 游说将 2032 年奥运会赛艇比赛移至鳄鱼栖息的河流的报道后做出回应 吉娜·莱因哈特 (Gina Rinehart) 昨天回应了一份报道，称她曾游说一项有争议的计划，将 2032 年奥运会赛艇比赛移至罗克汉普顿的菲茨罗伊河，那里是咸水鳄鱼的自然栖息地。 《卫报》的本·斯密报道称，这一决定引起了强烈反对。汉考克勘探公司的发言人昨天在一份声明中表示：莱因哈特夫人几十年来一直是澳大利亚地区的大力支持者，她在信中表达的见解是为了概述举办奥运会赛事将为像罗克汉普顿这样的地区城镇带来的好处。地方城镇常常被遗忘。鉴于莱因哈特女士也是澳大利亚赛艇协会的赞助人，参与这项运动多年，而且她对昆士兰州非常了解，所以她会像其他类似的体育代表一样就此事提供见解也就不足为奇了。暗示她这样做是出于任何不可告人的动机或获得任何个人利益是完全错误的！海洋保护主义者表示，大规模的海洋公园扩建是海洋的“胜利” 海洋保护主义者表示，联邦政府计划大规模扩大两个偏远岛屿周围的海洋公园面积，这将是海洋的胜利。环境部长默里·瓦特 (Murray Watt) 今天早上宣布了政府
